facts.text: Pine Bend’s name comes from a bend in the Mississippi where tall white pines once stood, a detail noted in 1915 accounts.
Pine Bend once hosted a Dakota Sioux village led by Chief Medicine Bottle in the mid‑19th century before treaties relocated the band.
The Pine Bend Bluffs cover 1,300 acres of oak savannas, tall‑grass prairies, wetlands, and towering white pines, supporting endangered species like the rusty‑patched bumblebee.
Pine Bend Refinery, operated by Flint Hills Resources, is Minnesota’s largest oil processing plant, handling 375,000 barrels per day.
The refinery’s 45‑megawatt solar project, completed in 2023, is the largest single‑user solar installation in the United States.
Pine Bend’s bluffs rise up to 200 feet above the Mississippi, a dramatic feature formed by glacial and post‑glacial processes over the last 8,000 years.
